messages:
michael: FYI I hit a weird failure when running smoke against the new vendor checkpoint. Ingest accepted the archive but bench couldn't mount the prefix cache. Looks like layout mismatch + different artifact naming.

michael: Repro: `smoke-run --model vendor_new.tar.gz --prefetch` -> mounts fail: 'cache: no matching prefix for artifact hash'
tara: Can you paste a minimal log?
michael: ```
WARN ingest: generated artifact id md5:abc123 from vendor_new.tar.gz
ERROR bench: no cache hit for artifact md5:abc123 expected sha256:...
```
liam: Ugh, md5 vs sha256 again. Vendor delivers md5-based manifests. We should standardize on a canonical hash scheme in intake and map vendor hashes. Options: (a) canonicalize to sha256 in intake and rewrite caches, (b) accept multiple hash algos in smokecache index, (c) generate a manifest that lists multiple digests.
anita: We also saw different artifact layout names: vendor calls it `kv-index.bin`, runtime expects `kv_index`. We need a small naming map or a canonical manifest that states logical artifact names + physical paths. That avoids brittle filename heuristics.
liam: Agreed. Proposal: intake produces a normalized manifest proto and an "artifact catalogue" with entries: logical_name, path_in_archive, digest_sha256, size, kv_layout_tag. That way bench, runtime, and cache all talk the same logical names.
tara: Tradeoffs: rewriting archives in intake (to rename files) is heavy. But generating a manifest alone and keeping the archive untouched is cheap and sufficient if all components consult the manifest. We should make the manifest immutable and store alongside the archive in blobstore.
benchbot: bench-run 1751112240: 1 failure -> cache miss due to hash mismatch. link: https://bench.redwood.example/runs/1751112240 :mag:
michael: Also: we need semantic fields for "compatibility hints" like `kv_stride`, `kv_endian` and `supports_chunked_kv` so runtime can quickly decide "can serve" vs "needs translation". Keep these booleans/strings small.
anita: Yes and include a "compat_score" tag computed by intake (0-100) that encodes how many known flags match our preferred runtime kernels. This helps prioritize model owners for manual fixes.
liam: Implementation plan: I'll add a lightweight canonicalizer in intake that computes sha256 of sub-artifacts and emits a manifest JSON. No archive mutation. Runtime and bench will read manifest first; if missing, fall back to old heuristics but log a deprecation.
tara: We'll require model CI to produce a manifest for new registries and intake will auto-generate for legacy artifacts, emitting a warning and opening an owner ticket. Also decide: prefer sha256 but allow other digests in a list field.
michael: I'll draft a 1-page RFC: manifest schema (logical_name, path, digests[], kv_layout, seqlen_hist, quant_profile, compat_score), intake behavior, smokecache indexing rules. Reviewers: @tara @liam @anita
anita: I'll prototype a smoke-cache index change that can resolve both md5 and sha256 entries by looking them up via manifest digests and by canonical logical name.
liam: I'll add early runtime checks that fail-fast with clear diagnostics and include a hint to the manifest field to inspect. Example error: `runtime: incompatible kv_layout=v1 (expected v2) -> see manifest.artifact[kv_index].kv_layout`
opsbot: Meeting reminder: eng-ml RFC sync tomorrow 10:00 to finalize schema.
michael: Cool. I'll open the RFC + PR with example manifests and a tiny CLI tool `redwood-manifest` later today. Thanks! :rocket:
